summary:
Earth System Trend Detective is an interactive geospatial telemetry and scenario forecasting platform built on 43 years of NASA Landsat 4–9 satellite observations (1984–2026). Powered by a zero-copy Rust and Apache Arrow backend paired with an interactive PyDeck and Streamlit dashboard, it fuses four biophysical signals—surface water (NDWI), land surface temperature (LST), vegetation vigor (NDVI), and soil salinity (SI)—across a 4 km spatial grid.

To address the challenge of detecting slow-onset environmental shifts hidden beneath seasonal weather noise, the platform uses outlier-resistant Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) statistics, spatial despeckling, and damped Linearly Weighted Least Squares (LWLS) forecasting to isolate compound tipping points—such as Aral Sea desiccation, Lake Mead depletion alongside Las Vegas urban sprawl, and Alaskan glacier retreat—while letting communities and policymakers simulate 2035 climate and water-extraction trajectories before ecosystems collapse.
details:
What It Does & How It Works Earth System Trend Detective transforms 43 years of multi-spectral NASA Landsat satellite observations (1984–2026) into an interactive spatial early-warning and scenario-forecasting platform across a 4 km × 4 km global grid. Users scrub through annual composites and inspect compound environmental shifts across three contrasting ecological regimes: endorheic basin desiccation (Aral Sea), reservoir drawdown paired with urban heat-island expansion (Lake Mead & Las Vegas), and tidewater cryosphere retreat (Harvard & Columbia Glaciers).

The platform operates through a three-stage telemetry pipeline:

  1. Multi-Signal Fusion: Combines four biophysical indicators derived from Landsat surface reflectance and thermal infrared bands—Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI), Land Surface Temperature (LST), Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), and Salinity Index (SI).
  2. Outlier-Resistant Anomaly Engine: Establishes a 1984–1992 baseline using Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) Z-scores clamped with a physical noise floor, paired with historical water-body masking and 3×3 spatial majority despeckling to isolate genuine structural shifts from single-year weather spikes or sensor artifacts.
  3. Regime-Aware 2035 Stress Simulator: Applies a 10-year Linearly Weighted Least Squares (LWLS) model with damped-trend attenuation and physical saturation bounds to project best-, baseline-, and worst-case trajectories through 2035 with 95% prediction intervals.

Key Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Early Tipping-Point Detection: Reveals slow-onset, multi-variable feedback loops—such as rising land surface temperatures and soil salinization following water loss—years before irreversible ecological collapse.
  • Accessible Scenario Testing: Translates raw petabyte-scale Earth observation archives into an intuitive visual tool where urban planners, water managers, and citizens can test the 2035 consequences of upstream water extraction and climate warming without needing specialized GIS expertise.
  • Sub-Millisecond Responsiveness: Eliminates sluggish browser lag when scrubbing across four decades of multi-layer geospatial grids, making exploratory climate analysis genuinely interactive.

Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Backend & High-Performance Compute: Rust (arrow-rs, parquet, tokio, axum) for zero-copy columnar decoding and SIMD-accelerated statistical computation.
  • Data Storage & Formats: Apache Parquet (columnar compression) and Apache Arrow (in-memory zero-copy buffers).
  • Frontend & Geospatial Visualization: Python (Streamlit, PyDeck, NumPy, SciPy) for hardware-accelerated WebGL spatial grid rendering and interactive scenario controls.
  • NASA & Partner Data: NASA/USGS Landsat 4, 5, 7, 8, and 9 Collection 2 Level-2 Surface Reflectance and Thermal Infrared products (1984–2026).

What Makes Our Project Creative Instead of treating satellite indices in isolation or fitting naive straight-line extrapolations that produce unphysical runaway predictions, we combined systems-level software engineering (zero-copy Rust/Arrow memory pipelines) with physics-constrained statistics. By anchoring anomaly detection to historical land-cover masks, applying morphological despeckling, and damping decadal LWLS slopes toward physical saturation boundaries, our forecasts respect real-world thermodynamic and hydrological limits while remaining fast enough for live interactive simulation.

Key Factors Our Team Considered

  • Signal-to-Noise Integrity: Single-year El Niño droughts, cloud shadows, or near-zero variance in hyper-arid deserts can trigger false alarms under standard Z-scores; we solved this using MAD statistics and physical noise floors.
  • Physical Realism in Forecasting: Unconstrained exponential or linear projections quickly violate conservation laws (e.g., negative water coverage or unphysical temperatures), leading us to design damped LWLS curves with asymptotic saturation bounds.
  • Usability Across Audiences: Balanced rigorous scientific metrics (Z-scores, confidence bands, multi-index coupling) with intuitive color-coded spatial telemetry and real-time scenario sliders so both domain scientists and non-technical stakeholders can extract actionable insights immediately.
